transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington I'm Louise Schiavone.
Democrats say they are planning to focus on lowering costs and rooting out corruption when
they take control of the House and Senate in January.
And PR Sam Greenglass reports.
Democrats say first on their legislative agenda is restoring enhanced health subsidies and
reversing Medicaid cuts, reasserting authority over tariffs and trying to end the Iran war.
On these priorities, Democrats are aligned, but they'll need help from some Republicans
in the Senate and cooperation from President Trump.
Beyond this early agenda, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who's likely the next speaker
of the House, is promising bold dramatic change, though what that looks like is not totally
clear.
Some newly elected moderate Democrats are wary of over-promising and under-delivering, while
new crop of progressives warn against just tinkering around the edges.
A hundred-plus new members will begin arriving in D.C. for orientation this weekend.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Washington.
Republican Congressman Jeff Herd has won re-election in Colorado.
He could become the only Republican in Colorado's congressional delegation.
Colorado Public Radio's Stena Sieg reports.
Herd was touring flood damage in the southwest part of the state when he learned he had won
Colorado's third congressional district, fending off Democratic challenger Dwayne Romero.
It was an election dominated by Democrats.
I think there's a message for us as Republicans that we need to make sure we are focused on
what we need to focus on, and that's making sure that we're making life better for families
in western southern Colorado.
Recent floods have damaged hundreds of homes in Herd's district.
He and the rest of Colorado's congressional delegation have signed a letter requesting
federal disaster relief.
For NPR News, I'm Stena Sieg in Grand Junction, Colorado.
In the state of Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colombe could be poised to make history as
the first black U.S. Senator from his state since post-Civil War Reconstruction.
There's still no official call on the race.
Colombe's vote count is around 2,500 ahead of incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde Smith.
Paraguay's former president appeared before the country's prosecutors after he was removed
from office and arrested yesterday over a bank scandal leaving millions without access
to their money, Catherine Osborne reports.
Santiago Pena, impeached as Paraguay's president on Friday, was a close ally of President Trump.
He was known as a pro-market leader focused on making it easier to do business in the
country.
But investigations allege he was too friendly to a large digital bank, which broke regulations
and collapsed.
It left millions of people blocked from their savings and triggered street protests.
A trial is proceeding against Pena, while his former vice president Pedro Aliana was
sworn in as president.
The U.S. embassy said it looks forward to working with him.
For NPR News, I'm Catherine Osborne in Rio de Janeiro.
This is NPR.
Soft robots might one day squeeze into crevices to explore shipwrecks and conduct search and
rescue operations, as Ari Daniel reports researchers are studying the octopus as a source of inspiration.
Aside from a rigid capsule around the brain and a small hard beak used for eating, the
octopus is entirely deformable.
People are fascinated by the escape artist aspect of octopuses.
Vienna Zoo biologist Tamar Gutnik and her colleagues observed octopuses transiting through
different sized holes.
The animals consistently inserted a single arm and then a few more.
They then used those arms to pull the rest of the body across.
With small holes, the common octopus compressed its body cavity and internal organs to squeeze
through.
Next up is the difficult task of building a robot that mimics the behavior of the octopuses.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
Two skydivers collided mid-air at an organized event in Lake Elsinore, California and fell
to the ground.
The accident occurred yesterday.
The Riverside County Fire Department said the two had suffered traumatic injuries and
were taken to a local hospital in critical condition, pronounced dead at the hospital.
Skydive Elsinore says as they were preparing to land, the two skydivers collided.
Their parachutes became entangled at approximately 150 feet above the ground.
Showers and thunderstorms move into southwestern Texas today, increasing the risk of flash
flooding in the Pacific Northwest, an active storm track will ramp up with soaking rains
and very high snow levels.
I'm Louise Kiavone, NPR News, Washington.

Republican Congressman Jeff Hurd wins reelection in Colorado's third district amid flood damage
Democrat Scott Colombe leads Senator Cindy Hyde Smith in Mississippi, possibly making history
Paraguay's former president Santiago Peña removed from office and arrested over bank scandal
Octopus escape behavior inspires soft robot design, researchers at Vienna Zoo report
